Ayodhya Kand.222: Ram rested, bathed at night, and then departed with Sita and Lakshman, bowing their heads to the joyful sages.
Ayodhya Kand.223: Ram lovingly asked the sages, "Lord, tell us which path we should take." The sages smiled in their hearts and said to Ram, "All paths are easy for you." The sages called their disciples to accompany them. Hearing this, fifty came with joyful hearts. All had immense love for Ram. All said, "Our path is visible." The sages then gave four young Brahmins to accompany them, who had accumulated good deeds in many births. Bowing and receiving the sages' permission, Ram departed with a joyful heart. When they approached a village, men and women rushed to see them. They felt blessed and fulfilled in their lives, but returned with sorrowful hearts when Ram departed.
Ayodhya Kand.224: Parting, Buti and Binay went, I remain, my mind engaged in work. Rising to bathe, Jamu found the water dark, matching her bodys hue.
Ayodhya Kand.225: Listening, the forest-dwelling man and woman. They forgot their own tasks. Lakhn, Ram, Sita, and Sundaratai. Seeing, they enhanced their own fortune. Extremely eager, their minds were restless. Whether singing or farming, they understood. When they lay together in embrace. They recognized Ram through his tricks. The whole story was narrated in the morning. They became engaged and went to live together. Hearing, they regretted everything. The queen Ray thought she was good. Then, a sage arrived. With fiery power, he persuaded. The poet, unrecorded, was a passionate devotee. Mind in order, loving Ram.
Ayodhya Kand.226: With tearful eyes and a body bristling with joy, recognizing his chosen deity, he fell to the ground like a stick; his condition cannot be described.
Ayodhya Kand.227: Ram lovingly embraced him with a thrilled heart, as if he had found the philosopher's stone, as if supreme love and ultimate truth had taken form and met, saying everything. Then Lakshman touched his feet. Ram lifted him with surging affection. Again, Sita placed the dust of his feet on her head. Knowing him as a son, she gave blessings. Nishad bowed to him. Ram's beloved met him joyfully. Drinking the nectar of his form with their eyes, they were as pleased as a hungry person finding good food. "Tell me, friend, how were those parents who sent them to the forest?"
Ayodhya Kand.228: Then Raghubir taught Dinesh many ways, guiding him. Dinesh wore Rams garland and went to meet him.
Ayodhya Kand.229: Again, Siya embraced Ram and Lakhna. Jamuna bowed before them. The sisters went happily with their two brothers. They made a great celebration with Rabinu and Jana. Many travelers met on the way. The two brothers saw the love and went on. Raj Lakhna saw all his limbs with you. Seeing, their hearts were very happy. They followed the path and found the way. Their shadows were false. The path was heavy with the forest of Giri. There, the sister was a young maiden. They became a couple and did not regret. Wherever they went, they reached there. Then, you were before them.
Ayodhya Kand.230: This way the question of love whispers in the ear of the eye. With gentle words, Binīt sits beside the ocean of mercy.
Ayodhya Kand.231: Jai Pur village is where Maahi resides. It is a place of serenity and joy. Some are virtuous, some are householders. Blessed is this land of purity and supreme bliss. Wherever Ramas footsteps tread, it is akin to Amaravati. The inhabitants of this land of merit are worthy of praise. Those who gaze upon Ramas eyes, accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana, are dark in hue. Where Rama resides, the deity of the river pays homage. Wherever the Lord sits, he makes a banyan tree grow. Ramas lotus feet are adorned with the earth, which acknowledges its vast share.
Ayodhya Kand.232: Smiling, the clouds pour rain; the mind is filled with joy. Seeing the mountains turn into a forest, the deer and Rama move on.
Ayodhya Kand.233: Sita and Lakhan entered Raghurajs village. When Nika entered, everyone heard. All the children and elders forgot their household chores. Rama and Lakhan saw Sitas form. Their eyes sparkled with joy. Their eyes filled with emotion, both heroes were captivated. The king could not approach them. He remained standing, his face red with anger. Each said one word and taught them. With their eyes and hands, they showed everything. Seeing Rama, a single affection arose. They walked, attached to each other. A single glance brought a picture to their heart. They became calm, body and mind.
Ayodhya Kand.234: A single glance is better than a cool breeze on soft grass. Say that work is done in the morning.
Ayodhya Kand.235: A kalash full of water. Anant Nath speaks in gentle words. On hearing, the beloved appears with excessive affection. Ram Karpolesu, the gentle and special. Knowing the toil of the heart, it remains within. Wishing to delay at home, but the heart longs. Happy women and men see beauty. Form unmatchable, eyes captivating. All see only him, the other is nowhere. Ramachandras face is the moon, the parrot. Young tamarind trees, body beautiful. Seeing crores of Madan, the heart is entranced. Damanini, becoming Lakhan, sweetly. Nails, beautiful, thoughts of joy. Muni Pat, how to cut the eye. Making the lotus a bow, the arrow is beauty.
Ayodhya Kand.237: The charming pair cannot be described. Their beauty is beyond my words. Ram, Lakshman, Sita's beauty captivated everyone's mind and intellect. Men and women, thirsty with love, were tired, as if deer seeing a mirage. The village women approached Sita. They hesitated to ask due to immense affection. They repeatedly touched her feet. Some spoke soft, simple words. "Princess, we make a request. We are hesitant to ask something due to our nature. Mistress, forgive our impertinence. Do not mind, knowing us to be ignorant. Royal work."
Ayodhya Kand.238: The beautiful Sumana, like the young Gauri. The face like the moon of the autumn night, eyes like autumn lotuses.
Ayodhya Kand.239: "O beautiful-faced one, who shames millions of Kamadevas, tell us who are these with you?" Hearing these affectionate and charming words, Sita smiled shyly in her heart. Looking at them, and then looking at the ground, the beautiful-bodied one was shy with double modesty. Shyly and lovingly, the fawn-eyed one spoke sweet words like a cuckoo: "By natural disposition, with beautiful fair bodies, their name is Lakshman, my younger brother-in-law." Then, covering her moon-like face with the edge of her garment, she looked at her husband's body with a sidelong glance. With beautiful, slightly tilted eyes like a wagtail, Sita indicated her husband to them with her gestures. All the village women were delighted, as if a poor person had plundered a king's treasure.
Ayodhya Kand.240: O most beloved, As she clasps thy neck in many ways, As she ever was the bride, When thou art pressed to her bosom, O beauty of the world.
Ayodhya Kand.241: Parbati is very fond of her. Devi does not have any equal. Punini brings her joy alone. Jauṁ is the path that leads to her. Darasanu, the god, knows her as his servant. Lakhini, all the beauties, are in love with her. Madhur speaks sweetly. Janu, Kumudini, and Kauṁudini, are all pleasing. Tabahin, Lakhan, knows Raghubar as a tree. Pūṁcheu, Magu, speaks gently to the people. Sunat, the woman, hears the mans sorrow. Pulakit, the observer, sings often. Mitha modu, the sweet taste, is in the heart.
Ayodhya Kand.242: Lakhan Janaki with Raghunath went to govern. Recited words of love for all dear ones, taking along his heart.
Ayodhya Kand.243: A wandering woman, a very settled man. In his faults, he sees himself in his mind. Together, they complain to each other. By fate, everything is reversed. Unblemished, without blemish, without anxiety. As if in a garden, all is serene. A dry tree, a forest of leaves, a sea of flowers. Thus, he reads and becomes a prince. When he becomes like this, he builds a home. He enjoys life by fate. He wanders, without a path, yet creates many paths. He is entangled in fate, yet stands firm. The wise creator brings forth beauty. Thus, he builds a home on this. He decorates and decorates, working hard. He is entangled in fate, yet stands firm. The wise creator brings forth beauty. Thus, he builds a home on this. He decorates and decorates, working hard.
Ayodhya Kand.244: O holy sage, adorned with a complex and beautiful matted hair, decorated with various kinds of ornaments, O Creator.
Ayodhya Kand.245: I have not tasted the root of the sweet potato. I have not heard the sound of the bell or seen the sight of the mirror. One speaks naturally, pleasingly. One remains unadorned, unadorned. Wherever the bed is laid, wherever the path is made. Hearing with ears, seeing with eyes, thinking with mind. Looking for, finding, eight or ten. Where is this man, where is this woman. Seeing this, the heart is filled with love. Becoming a yogi, he was transformed. Much effort was made, yet nothing was gained. Thus, he became irises, enduring hardships. We do not know much, but we honor what we have. Again, we write the ocean of merit. Where we see, where we see, what we see.
Ayodhya Kand.246: Saying thus, thus remaining alive, dear one, I fill my eyes with tears. How does he walk, this path unattainable, youthful and slender body.
Ayodhya Kand.247: Love for a woman is like a fleeting flower. By evening, one should sleep. The soft lotus petal knows the hard truth. The hearts secrets are like hidden words. But the gentle touch of the morning sun. Makes a mans heart like his own. When Jagadish created these, no suman could lead the way. When I met by fate, I saw my friend in my eyes. When neither man nor woman nor opportunity comes. Then Sita and Rama cannot be seen. When I heard the beauty of Surup, I understood Akulai. Now I am attached, where I am attached. Striving, I looked up to the sky. Then happy, I saw the fruits of life.
Ayodhya Kand.248: Women, children, and old people rubbed their hands in regret. Thus, people became bound by love wherever Ram went.
Ayodhya Kand.249: Village by village, they are full of joy. Seeing the sun, the caravan of Bhānukul moves on. Those who hear some news. They consider kings and queens as friends. Say, there is one very good person. We all love his eyes. Say, people love each other. Conversations are simple, affectionate. And those whose parents are blessed, may they go where they please. Blessed is that city where they come. Blessed is that country that makes them. Wherever they go, that is blessed. Finding happiness, they arrange it themselves. As if everyone is like that, full of affection. Rām Lakhn speaks of the path and story. All around, it is like a forest of listeners.
Ayodhya Kand.250: This way, the Ragukul Kamal Rabindranath gives happiness to the people. They see and go, including Bipin Sisy Samitri.
Ayodhya Kand.251: Ramu became front, Lakhan at the back. Tapas Beshi was aglow nearby. How Sitadevi stays in between both? Like Brahman and living beings, Maya in between. Truly I say, the picture that the mind stays in. Janu is in the midst of Madhu and Madan, entangled. Again I say, the comparison is like life and love. Janu is like Budh and Bidhu, Rohini in between. Lords feet are the line, Sita in the middle, all move. Sitas Ramas feet are marked as two. Lakhan moves to the right, taking the other two. Rama and Lakhans love for Sitadevi is clear. How to describe it, like the untraceable. Seeing the picture, the deer and the hunter. Taking the thiefs picture, Rama is marked.
Ayodhya Kand.252: Those who saw the dear companion Cy along with the two brothers. Life is without end, without end, without toil it remains unfulfilled.
Ayodhya Kand.253: Even today, in whose heart Lakshman, Sita, and Ram reside even in dreams, he will find the path to Ram's abode, which even some sages rarely find. Then, knowing Sita to be tired, Raghubir saw a banyan tree nearby with cool water. Residing there, they ate roots, tubers, and fruits. In the morning, after bathing, Ram departed. Seeing beautiful forests, lakes, and water, the Lord came to Valmiki's ashram. Ram saw the beautiful dwelling of the sage, with beautiful mountains, forests, and sacred water. Lotuses bloomed in the lakes, and trees in the forest. Charming bees, intoxicated with nectar, hummed. Birds and deer made a great clamor. Those who were enemies lived together peacefully and grazed with joyful hearts.
Ayodhya Kand.254: Seeing the beautiful Sukha Sundar Ashram, I was delighted with Rajivan. Hearing of Raghubars arrival, the sage came forward to greet him.
Ayodhya Kand.255: Muni said to Ram, bowing down. In Asiribad, the Brahmin was seen. Seeing this, Ram joined his eyes together. Then, with a garland, he went to the hermitage. The Muni received the guest, the dear one. He ate the sweet roots, fruits, and honey. Sita and Sumitra ate the fruit with Ram. Then, the Muni gave the hermitage as a gift. Valmikis heart was filled with joy. He saw the auspicious form with his eyes. Then, with a loud voice, he praised Raghuraam. He said, listening is a blissful act. You are the seer of the three ages, O Muni. Like the sun, you are in everyones hands. Saying this, the Lord narrated all the stories. As they were, so were the queens.
Ayodhya Kand.256: Father lives again for the sake of mother, brother saves the brother. I say that your Lord is all my good fortune and brilliance.
Ayodhya Kand.257: Seeing and bowing to Munira, may all our good deeds bear fruit. Now where Raur has become arid, Muni Udbe cannot find any. Muni and Tapasvin who bear pain, Without Nares, cannot find a supporter. Mangal Mool Bhritya, Paritoshu, Crores of families, Bhusuroshu. Knowing this, where should I go and stay? With Suyodhana and Sauti, wherever I go. There, arrange beautiful and fragrant grass. Do something kind and merciful for a while. Hearing the simple and sweet words of Raghubar, The Muni, a sage, spoke in praise. Who can say about this Raghu Kula? You are the sustainer, continuous, and the bridge of hearing.
Ayodhya Kand.258: Ram, you are the bridge of the Vedas, the protector, the Lord of the universe, and Janaki is your Maya. She who creates, sustains, and destroys the world, by the grace of the ocean of compassion. Lakshman, who is the thousand-headed serpent, the supporter of the earth, the master of all animate and inanimate beings. For the work of the gods, he has taken a royal body on earth and gone to crush the army of wicked demons.
Ayodhya Kand.259: Ram's form is dark, beyond words, beyond intellect. The Vedas say "not this, not this" about the unmanifest, indescribable, boundless one.
Ayodhya Kand.260: O ye gazers, I am the watcher. By the will of Hari, Harishchandra dances for you. Truly, no one knows you as you know. And you know none as you know yourself. So know that which you give to know. Your world is you and you are it. O Raghuveer, with your grace, you are the Bhagat and the Chandan. Your body is filled with consciousness and bliss, the master of speech and action. Wearing a body, the saints perform their work. What to say, the king of natural glory. I have seen and heard your story, O wise and happy. Whatever you say, I accept all. For the glory of the Jas.
Ayodhya Kand.261: Why do I ask where I am? If there is no there, give me where I can see for myself.
Ayodhya Kand.262: Hear O sage, of loves essence I sing, My heart with Ramas name in ecstasy fling. Bālamihi laughs, saying in delight, Sweet are thy words, O honey-sweet delight. O Rama, now what shall I say to thee? Where thou dwellest, Sita and Lakshmana be. Their ears are like the ocean vast and deep, Their stories, fair and manifold, I keep. Unending, ever flowing, never full, Their words, O home, I call their dwelling, true. Eager-eyed, they keep, Wishing to see, their gaze fixed, like a mirror true. Laid down, rivers Sindhu and Sar, Forming points, drops, and waves of blissful hue. Their hearts, abodes of joy and bliss, Ramas friend, Sita, and Raghunāyak, with
Ayodhya Kand.263: As thou art like the pure milk of the white swan, so doth Rama dwell in thy heart. Wearing the diadem of praise, he dwelleth in thy soul.
Ayodhya Kand.264: Lords grace is fortunate and blessed. With humility, we receive it daily. You have offered us food, Lords grace is like a crown. Seeing the new, hearing the gurus wisdom, you are special with affection. Continuously worship the feet of Rama. Rama is trust in the heart, no other. Travel the pilgrimage of Rama. Rama resides in their heart. Always chant your mantra, worship with your family. Perform various rituals and offerings as per the rules. You are more than a guru, known and served by all.
Ayodhya Kand.265: Sell a fruit and go to meet Rama Charn. There in my heart, the temple of Sita and Rama remains.
Ayodhya Kand.266: Work is truth, wealth is deceit. Greed is not, nor is anger or enmity. Those who have no deceit, no pretense, no illusion. Their hearts dwell in Raghuraja. All are dear, all are benefactors. Pain and joy, both are songs of praise. Speak the truth, be dear, think of survival. Awake when sleeping, seek refuge in you. You are the only way, there is no other way. Rama dwells in their hearts. Mother is like a sister, wife is like a stranger. Poison is heavy, even poison is heavy. Who sees wealth beyond joy, becomes sad in adversity. Those who you are the breath of life, their hearts dwell in your abode.
Ayodhya Kand.267: O my brothers, my parents, my guru, I owe everything to you. My hearts temple, let those two lands reside with peace.
Ayodhya Kand.268: Fault conceals others merits. A Brahmin bears hardships for the good of others. A wise person adapts to any situation. Your home is where your heart finds peace. Your merits are understood by your closest. As everyone trusts you in the same way. Lord Ram is dear to devotees. So He resides in their hearts affectionately. Family, lineage, wealth, and righteousness are great. A dear family is a happy gathering. You are with them in your heart. Their hearts remain attached to you. Good and bad, virtuous and sinful, are all the same. Wherever you look, you see the truth. Good deeds, life, and death are all connected. Devotees do as Lord Ram does. So He remains in their hearts.
Ayodhya Kand.269: I never felt any hesitation or reluctance towards you. I constantly dwell in you, my heart ever immersed in you.
Ayodhya Kand.270: Thus, the sages showed the temple. Living in love with Ram, they enjoyed in their hearts. O sage, tell us, Lord of the sun. Say, my sage, where is your ashram? It brings joy with its time. Dwelling in the Chitrakoot hill, they lived as you do. The forest is lovely with sal trees. There, deer play and frolic. The river is pure and old, praising Atiripriya, her own ascetic power. The Mandakini stream flows like Sursar. It calls out every sin and vice. The sages, including Atri, have lived many. Practicing yoga, japa, and penance. Going forth, successful labor, they do all. Give us the honor, Lord of the mountains, Ram.
Ayodhya Kand.271: The glory of Chitrakuta is limitless, O great sage Agni. Whether they come or bathe, the river Saraswati and the two brothers are there.
Ayodhya Kand.272: Raghubar said, "Lakshman, find a good place. Now describe the suitable spot." Lakshman gave a firm reply. He turned in all four directions like a bowman. "The river, trees, arrows, self-control, restraint, charity, all kinds of impurities of Kali Yuga, and various evils. Chitrakoot is like an immovable hunter. It does not miss its target in a close fight." Saying this, Lakshman showed the place. Seeing the spot, Raghubar was pleased. Ram, knowing the minds of the gods, departed with Sita, the chief architect of the gods. Kol and Kirat tribesmen all came in their attire. They built beautiful leaf-huts. The two charming halls cannot be described. One was small and beautiful, the other large.
Ayodhya Kand.273: Lakhan Janaki with Prabhu Rajat Ruchira Niket. Soham Madanu Muni in love with Janu Rati Rituraj at that time.
Ayodhya Kand.274: Gods, Nagas, Kinnaras, and guardians of directions came to Chitrakoot at that time. Ram bowed to everyone. The gods were delighted and gained the benefit of seeing him. Showering flowers, the assembly of gods said, "Lord, today we have found our protector." Making their pleas and narrating their unbearable sorrows, they happily returned to their abodes. Raghunandan resided in Chitrakoot. Hearing the news, sages came. Seeing the multitude of joyful sages arriving, the moon of the Raghu clan bowed to them. The sages embraced Raghubar in their hearts. They gave blessings for his well-being. Sita and Saumitra's beauty made all their spiritual practices fruitful.
Ayodhya Kand.275: The sages, having paid respects to the lord and bid farewell, continued their yoga, japa, vigil, and tapas in their own ashrams.
Ayodhya Kand.276: This good fortune came to Kiratan. Joyfully, wealth entered the home. Roots and fruits filled the basket. Went to the market, and Janu won gold. Those who saw the two brothers were pleased. The other came to know by asking. Raghubir left, saying and hearing Raghurani. Holding joy, they went forward. The Lord looked with great affection. Janu wrote, wherever he went, his heart throbbed. Love for Rama was felt by all. Said dear, stay, be the honor of all times. The Lord was pleased, saying and doing.
Ayodhya Kand.277: Now we have become Nath Sanath and behold the Lord. Our coming is for liberation, O Cosalraiy.
Ayodhya Kand.278: Blessed is the land, the path, the mountain. Wherever you find the master, there flows the stream. Blessed are the deer, the forest dwellers. You have made our lives prosperous, we see with our own eyes. We are all blessed, a family together. We see with our eyes filled with your vision. These dwellings are good, these places are considered. Here all seasons bring happiness. We serve as servants, as laborers. We work, we toil, like the bees. Becoming independent, the mountains and valleys are tamed. We are all your servants, we prostrate before you. You play wherever you are, you are the one who sees through the difficulties. We are the servants of the family, the master does not get angry, he accepts.
Ayodhya Kand.279: The Lord, the abode of compassion, whose words are unfathomable to the minds of sages. Hearing the words of the Kiratas, like a father hearing the words of his child.
Ayodhya Kand.280: Rama only loves love. Knowing the way to know. Rama becomes all in all in those days. Saying softly, living on love. Bowing, not going away. Lord sings praises, coming to hear at home. Thus, Sita and the two brothers. Living in happiness, singing, contented sages. When Raghunath came, then fear turned into auspiciousness. Flowers and fruits, various ways. Beautiful, fragrant, hanging. Beautiful faces, beautiful bodies, pleasing. Mind becoming restless, coming to remove. Splendid, beautiful, honey-like classes. Threefold beauty, bringing happiness.
Ayodhya Kand.281: Peacocks, cuckoos, parrots, chatakas, chakravakas, and chakoras. Birds of various kinds sing, pleasing to the ears and captivating the mind.
Ayodhya Kand.282: Elephants, lions, monkeys, boars, and deer. All wander together without fear. Seeing the beauty of the hunting grounds, the deer in the forest become especially joyful. Wherever there are divine forests in the world, all of them envy Ram's forest. The Ganga, Saraswati, Yamuna, Narmada, Godavari are blessed. All lakes, oceans, rivers, and streams of various kinds. They praise the Mandakini. The Udaya and Asta mountains, Kailash, Mandar, Meru, all abodes of gods. All mountains like Himachal and others, they all sing the glory of Chitrakoot. The mind is so joyful that happiness cannot be contained. They have attained great glory without effort.
Ayodhya Kand.283: The deer, vines, trees, and grasses of Chitrakoot's forest. All are heaps of merit, thus say the gods day and night.
Ayodhya Kand.284: The resplendent Raghubar has seen the light. May the fruit of life be bountiful. Changeable is the mortal, but eternal is bliss. Become the rightful heir to the supreme position. So be fair and kind, pleasing and charming. Most auspicious, extremely sanctified. Praise be to the poet who thus spoke. A haven in the ocean of bliss. The boundary of Ayodhya has been left behind. Where Sita, Lakhan, and Rama dwelt. Even the most beautiful forest cannot compare. Thousands of times more beautiful. So I shall speak as I am bidden. I will not hide behind the mandara flower. Serving Lakhan, performing acts of kindness, with heart and soul. Going, I shall not be a cold or unloving breeze.
Ayodhya Kand.285: Chinu write Siya Rams feet knowing them. Do not dream to see Chitu, brother, mother, father.
Ayodhya Kand.286: Ram sang with Sita, they lived in happiness. A pure and noble family, they cherished beauty. They saw each other as brothers and sisters, their hearts filled with joy like swallows. Tears never flowed, they were happy like crows every day. Sitas heart was filled with love for Rams footsteps. In Avad, she became as dear as a thousand lifetimes. In the beloveds company, she found joy in her beloved and family. Mothers, fathers, and wise men were like roots and fruits. Lord and companion, they were companions in happiness. People looked up to them, as if they could enjoy the world.
Ayodhya Kand.287: Remember Ram, when men lived like blades of grass in bliss. Rams beloved, the mother of the world, Sita did not behave even a little like that.
Ayodhya Kand.288: Sita and Lakshman, who find happiness in any way. That is what Raghunath does and says. He tells ancient tales and stories. Lakshman and Sita listen with great joy. When Ram remembers Ayodhya, his eyes fill with tears. Remembering his mother, father, family, and brother Bharat's affection, character, and service. The Lord, ocean of mercy, becomes sorrowful. He holds patience, considering the adverse time. Seeing this, Sita and Lakshman become distressed, just as a shadow follows a person. Seeing the state of his dear brother, Raghunandan, the patient, compassionate one, who is like sandalwood to the hearts of devotees, began to narrate some sacred stories. Hearing them, they found happiness.
Ayodhya Kand.289: Ramu Lakhan with Seeta at Sohat Paran Niket. Jimi Bas in Amarpur with Sachee Jayanti.
Ayodhya Kand.290: The Lord, Sita, and Lakshman are united like the eyelids and the pupils of the eyes. Lakshman serves Sita and Raghubir, just as an ignorant person serves his body. In this way, the Lord resides happily in the forest, benefiting birds, animals, gods, and ascetics. Now, hear, Sumant, how Ram's beautiful departure to the forest came to Ayodhya. The Nishad returned after escorting the Lord. He saw the chariot arrive with the minister. The minister, seeing the Nishad, became distraught. The sorrow that arose could not be described. He cried out for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. He fell to the ground, greatly agitated. Seeing the horses neighing towards the south.
Ayodhya Kand.291: Not a blade of grass moves, not a drop of water quivers, the eyes glisten with dew. The Nishad, startled, gazes at the battle of Raghus lineage.
Ayodhya Kand.292: With patience, the bowman spoke then. Now Sumitra should advise the hesitant. You are a scholar, aware of great matters. Hold your patience, understand, and speak gently to the fickle creator with various stories. Sit in the chariot, waiting for the arrival. The sorrow settled, the chariot could not groan. Raghubirs absence pained his heart. Back and forth, yet moving not in fear. As a deer, his mind came, the chariot moved with force. Hesitating, then looking back. Sorrow of separation, like a wound, pierced his heart. Who speaks of Rama, Lakshmana, Baidéhi. Thinking, thinking, finding benefit in the thought. The passage of separation, how can it be described. Without mind, it twists, like what it is.
Ayodhya Kand.294: Guha returned after escorting the chariot. His separation and sorrow could not be described. The Nishad drove the chariot towards Ayodhya. Moment by moment, he was immersed in sorrow. Sumant, distressed and sorrowful, thought, "This life is long without Raghubir. This vile body will not remain in the end. I will not gain fame by separating from Raghubir. My life has become a vessel of infamy and sin. For what reason does it not depart? Alas, my foolish mind missed the opportunity. Even now, my heart does not break into pieces. He wrung his hands and beat his head in regret. Like a miser who has lost a heap of wealth in his mind. His reputation was bound."
Ayodhya Kand.295: He thinks while weighing the pros and cons as a secretary.
Ayodhya Kand.296: Just as a noble, virtuous, and wise woman, devoted to her husband in deed, thought, and word, remains under the control of her actions and falls into the hands of her husband. Similarly, a terrible burning was in the minister's heart. His eyes were tearful, his sight diminished. His ears could not hear, his mind was bewildered. His lips were dry, his mouth parched. His life would not leave his deceitful heart. He became discolored, unable to be looked at. As if his father and mother had been killed. Great shame and sorrow spread in his mind. He worried about the path to Yamapur like a sinner. Words did not come, his heart regretted. He thought, "I will go and see Ayodhya. Seeing the chariot without Ram, everyone will be ashamed to look at me."
Ayodhya Kand.297: When the tail is lifted, I am with the men and women of the city at noon. I will go and stay with them every morning, making my heart resonate.
Ayodhya Kand.298: Ask Mother, who is poor and sorrowful. Why should I be the one to comfort her? Ask when I shall meet Mahatari. Why should I be the one to convey the message? When Mother Rama came to give birth, remember the child like a calf was brought. I ask and return, giving, Rama and Lakhan as a bride. When I ask, I return, giving. Go to Avadh now and take pleasure. When I ask, sorrow comes to the poor. Live under the rule of Raghunath. Who should I ask to bring me? I came to Kusala, Kuan, to meet. Listening to Lakhan, Sita and Ramas message. I left like a blade of grass, leaving the body.
Ayodhya Kand.299: The lake does not weep for the bank where the reed sways, and Pritham (meaning of Niri is unclear without context) does not weep. I know that in this way lies the path of departure of the body.
Ayodhya Kand.300: By this path, one attains knowledge. The iron of darkness immediately turned into light. Saying goodbye, the kind hunter went. Returning at midnight, he was filled with sorrow. The city official was beaten up. The king cursed him like a snake. Sitting and gnawing his fingers, he spent the day. Evening came, providing an opportunity. The darkness of exile began. Keeping the house and gate, he prayed. Those who heard the news came to the kings gate. Recognizing the chariot at midnight, he was terrified. Crying like a burning one. The city men and women were frightened. They gathered like fish in a pond.
Ayodhya Kand.301: Councillor Sunat heard Sabu at five in the evening. The house feels like the residence of a ghost, and indeed it does.
Ayodhya Kand.302: Exceeding all praise, the queen has a long tail. She does not move, becoming silent. Hearing does not make the eyes understand. Saying where the king is, one understands. Seeing the minister, the queen went to her house. Going to Sumitra to see which king, Chandu was agitated. Seated on a bed, adorned with nothing, lying on a mat, worn out. Taking this thought, thinking in this way, Surapuras people were humiliated. Thinking and thinking, tearing and tearing her clothes. As if wings, she moved. Saying Ram, loving Ram. Again saying Ram, Lakhan, a beauty.
Ayodhya Kand.303: Seeing the minister, Jay Jiiva said, We bow in submission to the punishment. The king, startled upon hearing this, asked Sumitra, Where is Ram?
Ayodhya Kand.304: The King embraced Sumant. As if a wise man had received some respect. He seated him near with affection. The King asked, his eyes filled with tears, "Tell me, dear friend, about Ram's well-being. Where are Raghunath, Lakshman, and Vaidehi? Did you bring them back, or did they proceed to the forest?" Hearing this, the minister's eyes filled with water. Distraught with sorrow, the King again asked, "Tell me the message of Sita, Ram, and Lakshman." Remembering Ram's form, qualities, character, and nature, the King worried in his heart. The King had pronounced the exile. Hearing this, his mind became.
Ayodhya Kand.305: Friend Ramu Siya Lakhnu wherever they are I will reach. No longer do I wish to wander now I say life is Satibai.
Ayodhya Kand.306: Again and again, the minister would ask Rao. Beloved, he would convey messages. Doing so, friend, he would become a beggar. Rama and Lakhan would show their eyes. The minister, calm, spoke in measured words. Great king, you are a learned scholar. Hero, wise, and steadfast god. Always serving the good and society. Life and death, all suffering will be endured. Gain and loss, meeting and separation of loved ones. Time and karma bind you, Gosain. Day and night, a constant balance. Joy and sorrow, roots of suffering are written. Both equal, calm, hold your mind. Calm, reflect, and be a wise counselor.
Ayodhya Kand.307: First blind, second clear and calm. Bathing, they performed penance with Sita, the two heroes.
Ayodhya Kand.308: Spring has many devotees. So the heart desires to serve Him. It is the morning hour, the time to rise. It is the time to make the headgear with ones own hair. O Ram, let my name be thy friend. I adorn my beloved with my own hair. I make a bow with my own hands. I see the Lord with my own eyes. I am captivated by Raghubir everywhere. I speak sweet words with patience. I prostrate to my father and say many things. I offer twelve lotus petals. I get up early in the morning without any sorrow. I know the pain of thinking of my father.
Ayodhya Kand.309: Through your grace, dear Kanai, I find all happiness. Seeing the protector and the good, I come again and again. Mother, full of joy, circles and circles, full of gratitude. Tulsidas begs to remain, as long as good fortune remains with Kosala.
Ayodhya Kand.310: The Gurus counsel and message are conveyed again and again through the lotus. The lesson is to remain steadfast, for those who do not think are rulers for a brief moment.
Ayodhya Kand.311: Brother is a complete companion. Father, listen to my apology. So I, like others, am a benefactor. Living, remain without sorrow. Messengers bring news, come with a message. Not following principles, do not reach the position of a king. Nourish your people with actions, your heart is the measure of everything. Or, keep brotherhood. Do service for your parents. Like this, always keep it. Thinking, I, like what I do not do. Lakhn says, what remains difficult. Standing by Rama, I again fell into illusion. Again and again, follow your own path. Lakhn, not like you, is a poet.
Ayodhya Kand.312: Saying namaskar, I can say nothing but that my affection has become gentle. Weary are my eyes, moist are my cheeks, my body is flushed with emotion.
Ayodhya Kand.313: That opportunity Raghubar saw. Kevat passed, the boat was rowed. Raghukulatilak went in this manner. I saw the tall backdrops touching the chest. I can say what calamity those backdrops brought. I will go back and convey the message to Rama. Thus said the minister Bhanu, thinking of loss and gain. Son Bhanu heard, the men weep. Beyond that, the heart burns with anger. The mind was overwhelmed by intense passion. The queen weeps, all lamenting great misfortune. Hearing the lament, the heart aches, one takes time to think.
Ayodhya Kand.314: The king heard the loud noise and commotion for a long time. At night, he realized the situation was severe.
Ayodhya Kand.315: Fear clings to the throat, terror seizes the heart. Mindless are the feet, agitated the steps. Indeed, all actions become heavy. Feet turn into waves, without rest. Sita saw the king, Rama in the forest, knew. Dheeraam bears the weight, calm and great. Speaks in due time, following the season. Understanding the Lord, the mind contemplates. Rama is beyond compare, in his absence. You carry the burden, the journey of life. Climb the path of all beloveds. Be calm, cross the river. Not with a family, but with all. Hold on, with no other, drink the nectar. Meet Rama, find Sita, in the journey of life.
Ayodhya Kand.316: Hearing the sweet and gentle words, the king's consciousness opened. Like a fish struggling in mud, longing for cool water.
Ayodhya Kand.317: With patience and composure, she rose and sat, sighing. Sumitra spoke, asking where Ram, the merciful one, was. Where was Lakhan, where was Ram, the beloved? Where was the dear son and daughter-in-law, the beautiful ones. The night was filled with various forms, the day seemed like a moment. The wise, the blind, and the serpent gained insight. Kausalya narrated all these stories. Fearful of the night, history was recited. Ram was absent, life was a dream. With this body, what can I do? Without love, I cannot live. This is Raghus joy, without you many days pass. This is Janaki, Lakhan, this is Raghubir, this is the water of desire for the heart.
Ayodhya Kand.318: Saying Rama, saying Rama, saying Rama, saying Rama. Abandoning his body, the king, due to separation from Raghuvir, went to the abode of the gods.
Ayodhya Kand.319: Dasaratha attained the fruit of glorious death. His pure fame spread in many ways. As Ram departed, he gazed at his moon-like face. Death due to separation from Ram became glorious. All the queens wept, distraught with sorrow. Praising his beauty, character, strength, and radiance. They lamented in many ways. Falling to the ground again and again. Servants and maids wept, distraught. Townspeople wept in their homes. Today, the sun of the solar dynasty has set. The embodiment of Dharma, a treasure of virtues and beauty. Everyone cursed Kaikeyi's body. Saying, "She has made the world blind." As they lamented in this manner, the night passed. All the great wise sages arrived.
Ayodhya Kand.320: Then Basishtha Muni said the history of many eras. Weep not, show sorrow no more from morning on your own light shine.
Ayodhya Kand.321: The king kept the body alive with the oil name. The messenger spoke again and again in that language. Begi ran and Bhar went to the cart. The king asked the people what wisdom they had and why they spoke. Thus, Begi kept going for many years. The guru spoke and the two brothers read. The sage and the mendicant ran and walked. Beg went to the battlefield and was ashamed. Uselessly the term of life began. They became bad because of bad deeds. One saw a terrifying dream at night and woke up with sharp imagination. The Brahmin gave a day and the god was bathed in various ways. The heart mourned for the great god. The bad mother and father were relatives.
Ayodhya Kand.322: This way of thinking and the heart running to reach. Following the gurus instructions, he listened and went meditating on Ganesh.
Ayodhya Kand.323: Samir Beg went to Haanki. Naagat Silit became a bank. Heart thinks big but does not agree. Without knowing, I go away flying. In a moment, it rains like summer. This way, the city is filled with water. The city becomes angry, shouting and quarreling. Saying opposite, they talk. Hearing, hearing, the heart is filled with sorrow. Srihat Silit became a garden. The city feels special and sad. The deer and bird did not come but went away. Ram biyog kurog bigo. The city, women, and men suffer. Everyone loses their wealth in the heart.
Ayodhya Kand.324: The townspeople will meet, but will not say anything, they will just look and go. Bharat will not be able to reach Kusal, fear and sorrow are in his mind.
Ayodhya Kand.325: Market does not go where Niharī looks. Janu Pur stays closed for the tenth day, waiting to be opened. Aavat Sut hears the name Kakayandini. Harshī and Rabikul are like the moon in the water. Saji Aarati is delighted and rises early. She meets Bhawan at the door and brings him inside. Bharat, seeing the distressed family, looks at Tuhiin and kills him. Kakay is delighted in this way. Thinking of the joy, she buys a Kirati dress. She sees her daughter and beats her. She asks Nahir if Kusali is ours. Bharat tells all this to Kusali. He asks where all mothers are. Where is Sita, Rama, Lakhan, and dear brother.
Ayodhya Kand.326: Hearing the sons affectionate deceitful words filled with honey, the eyes were filled with tears. The speakers ears, heart, and tongue all felt like they were pierced by needles, whether speaking or not.
Ayodhya Kand.327: Father speak I have gathered all. Fear not, I will consider the help. A little work by the way has been spoiled. Lord and God have taken their seats. Hearing this, Bharata became very sad. Janu, with his consent, began to weep. Father, I call you. Afraid of the earth, I am very agitated. I did not see where to go. Father, I cannot give you my hand. Calmly standing up, he gathered himself. Father says this is for my death. Hearing this, Suthe, the son, said to Kakei. I will die with you. Everything from the beginning is to be done by yourself. Shrewd, harsh, and fickle-minded, the mind should be changed.
Ayodhya Kand.328: Though the river flowed past, Ram became silent hearing of death. Knowing his own fate, he bore it in silence.
Ayodhya Kand.329: In the evening he explains and understands. If the mind is set on attachment. Then the father does not think of the son. Enjoying the fruits of deep good deeds. Living all life and experiencing all. At the end, the immortal king leads to salvation. Do not think of conjectures. Building a society and a royal city together. Listening quietly, the prince agrees. His body burns like a fire. With patience, he bears the heat. Like a sinner, he starts the day. Even if it is Kurus fault, why should I blame the people. Cutting the tree, I water it. The fish is caught, I blame the net.
Ayodhya Kand.330: Dasaratha of the solar dynasty is the father, Ram and Lakshman are brothers. You are the mother, mother, nothing is in the hands of fate.
Ayodhya Kand.331: When I see the beauty of youth, I forget my age. My heart is divided, yet I do not grow old. The pious man seeks his heart, but does not find it. The wise man does not touch the lips of the unwise. The king appears to be like others. Death is by destiny, wisdom is from God. Wisdom is the path of the heart, all deceit and flaws are to be avoided. Simple, virtuous, and righteous, one should remain steadfast. Such is the knowledge of her who is beautiful. All living beings in the world are known, those dear to Raghunath are not. You are extremely harmful to Ram, yet you claim to be truthful. Smiling, you smile, making me smile. Raising your eyes, you sit down.
Ayodhya Kand.332: The rebellious heart of the Rams is evident in this way; I am charmed. I cannot say much about one who is like me in guilt.
Ayodhya Kand.333: Hearing Satrughuns mothers cunning, when she sang but did not finish the song. That opportunity was Kubers, he came there. Wearing ornaments, he made various disguises. Writing and singing, Likhun, his younger brother, filled the song. Wearing incense and ghee, he offered prayers. Coming to Kuber, I struck him with a stick. But with my mouth, I called out to him. Kuber broke and fell apart. The Dasans faces were covered in blood. Ah, Ripun, I did not lose. I practiced my nails, one by one. Pressing the ocean of mercy, he left. Kausalya went to the two brothers.
Ayodhya Kand.334: Poor clothes torn and worn, body burdened with suffering. Like a golden necklace worn out, I realize my end is near.
Ayodhya Kand.335: Looking at Bharata, my mother rose and wept. The earth, faint and feeble, stood there. Seeing Bharata, the burden grew heavy. I forgot the toil of wandering with the others. My mother and brother showed me where. There I saw Sita, Rama, and the two brothers. Oh, how many lives have been mine on earth. Why, in so many lives, did I not remain steadfast? My lineage is stained, as in each life I have been unfaithful to my beloved. I am bewitched by the world, a wretched soul, as my mother clung to me. But Ramas city became Suryapur, and Raghuvamsha was established. I am only here for futile reasons. I am consumed by love, a flame, and suffer from pain, distress, and corruption.
Ayodhya Kand.336: The mother, hearing softly that Bharat was in danger, rose with care. She took and dressed his wounds, tear after tear.
Ayodhya Kand.337: Simple beauty brought me joy. Great love made my heart Ram return. Meeting often, Lakhn the younger brother. Suffering from affection, hearts did not merge. Seeing the beauty, Sabin said to some. Why Ram is not with you? Mother Bharat sat in her arms. Crying with her foot, softly she called out. Soon the child grew patient and wise. Understanding the flowers, sorrow was left behind. Knowing life brings loss and pain. Time of actions brings change. Sometimes the dear father gives life. I am the one who fulfills all. Who brings such pain and sorrow. Soon I will know the reason behind it.
Ayodhya Kand.338: Without joy the heart wore no ornament of pleasure.
Ayodhya Kand.339: Smiling face, joyous heart, not angry. Do everything with joy. Bipin came, hearing Sitas song, attached to Ramas form, lovingly. Lakhan, listening, came to join. Raghunath stayed, not doing anything. Then Raghupati, all day, had no time. Came with Sita, a small brother. Rama, Lakhan, and Sita became friends. Neither went with the group, nor lived. These are their faces, these are their eyes. You cannot hide, body and life are incomplete. I have no shame, my own eyes see me. Rama, my son, I am a great lady. Wherever I die, good king, know me. My heart is true, like the plot.
Ayodhya Kand.340: Kausalya, hearing that Bharata was alive, rushed to Rnivasa. Overwhelmed with joy, she forgot her sorrows and ran to the royal palace.
Ayodhya Kand.341: Bharat and his brother wept, distraught. Kausalya embraced them to her heart. Bharat consoled them in many ways. Speaking words full of wisdom. Bharat also consoled all the mothers. Narrating beautiful stories from Puranas and Shrutis. With a guileless, pure, simple, and sweet voice, Bharat spoke, joining his hands. "May those sins befall me, O Creator, which involve killing mother, father, or son. Burning cowsheds, villages of Brahmins. Killing women and children. Giving poison to a friend or king. All major and minor sins, which poets describe as born of action, word, and mind. May those sins befall me, O Creator, if this is my mother's intention."
Ayodhya Kand.342: Worship Hari, Hari, Har Charan; O terrible beings. There is no way to deceive Me; I know your birth mother.
Ayodhya Kand.343: Sell not the dharma, for it is precious; speak not evil of the virtuous. Cunning, deceitful, quarrelsome, angry, a breaker of the Vedas, a disturber of the world. Greedy, deceitful, fickle in behavior. He who looks at anothers wealth or wife. I shall follow the path of those three horrors. If my mother consents to it, so be it. He who does not love the company of the virtuous, turns away from the path of supreme bliss, unworthy. He who does not worship Hari, the jewel among men. If he does not love Hari, he loves not the true Hari. He who does not follow the path of the Vedas, is deceitful, a cheat, and a trickster in the world. He who follows the path of impurity and corruption, I shall follow his path. If my mother knows it, I shall go.
Ayodhya Kand.344: Mother Bharti heard that Sachi was simple and kind. She said to Ram, dear son, always think of staying safe in your heart.
Ayodhya Kand.345: You are dearer than life to Ram. You are dearer than life to Raghupati. Even if the moon emits poison, snow emits fire. Even if aquatic creatures become detached from water. Even if the sky falls, or delusion does not end. You should not be adverse to Ram. If this opinion of yours is what the world says. Then you will not attain happiness or good fortune even in dreams. Saying this, the mother embraced Bharat to her heart. Tears flowed from her breasts, her eyes filled with water. Lamenting much in this manner. The entire night passed while sitting. Then Vamadeva and Vashishtha arrived. All the ministers and prominent citizens were called. The sage instructed Bharat in many ways.
Ayodhya Kand.346: Father bear with patience the heart whatever opportunity comes today. Arise O filled with Guru listen to the call and put on all the decorations.
Ayodhya Kand.347: The prince is the essence of the Vedas, a wondrous aerial vehicle. Holding the earth on four feet, the queen desires to see the king. If the sandalwood is heavy with fragrance, countless scents please. Crafting a mirror with a smooth surface, the steps of Surapura are pleasing. Thus, all actions are performed in this manner, washing with skillful tila oil. Remembering the ancient Vedas, all are filled with wisdom. Where the sage has come, everything is done with devotion. Given as pure gifts, all are given in various forms, like cows, oxen, and elephants.
Ayodhya Kand.349: He filled his actions with goodness as he should. Such a face does not fade even if seen by a hundred eyes. Suddin, the wise and great, came when asked. All officials spoke together. Everyone went to the royal assembly. Bharat read and spoke to his two brothers. Bharat and Basistha sat close together. They spoke of duty and righteousness. First, the wise narrated the story. He performed as Kaki did deviously. Bhup praised the vow of duty, renouncing the body and embracing love. Saying good qualities of Ram, he had moist eyes and pleased the sages. Often, Lakhna expressed Siyas love. Sorrow and affection made the sages understand.
Ayodhya Kand.350: Listen O Bharat, the Muninath writes in future the strong with pen. Gain and loss in life, birth and death, by fates own design.
Ayodhya Kand.351: Without thinking, give something to a friend. Sleep some while crying and worrying. Think and meditate, but there is no king without a second thought. Think of a Brahmin who has no Vedas. He is attached to his own dharma and material possessions. Think of a king who does not know policy. One who is not dear to his people and not as precious as life. Think of a rich miser who is not kind to guests and does not know devotion. Think of a Sudra, a Brahmin, as low. Mocked and despised, knowledge is forgotten. Think again of a wife, a deceitful, quarrelsome, and desire-driven. Think of a boy who renounces his vow. He does not follow his guru.
Ayodhya Kand.352: Think of the home that is lost to passion, abandoning the path of virtue. Think of the nature devoted to renunciation, forsaking wisdom and detachment.
Ayodhya Kand.353: He who is worthy of praise is worthy of thought. He who abandons penance for future enjoyment. He who is a slanderer, causelessly angry. He who is hostile to mother, father, guru, and brother. He who is harmful in every way, a great nurturer of his own body, and very cruel. He who is without thought in every way. He who does not abandon deceit, even if he is a devotee of Hari. Do not think about the king of Kosala. O Lord, his glory is manifest in all fourteen worlds. There has not been, nor will there be, a king like your father Dasaratha. Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Indra, and the guardians of the directions. All describe the virtues of Dasaratha.
Ayodhya Kand.354: Tell Uncle to do something to show off. Ram Lakhn, you are your own enemy, think about it.
Ayodhya Kand.355: All kinds of kings are major shareholders. He who divides becomes one. Hearing this, understand and think, avoid. Hold the head and act as a king and queen. O king, your position is that of a poor man. You desire to be like your father. When Ram became such that he had to stay away, he avoided his body and became separated from Ram. A kings life is not dear to his beloved, his life. Holding the head, the king acts as a king and queen. You are all like this, doing well. But Parashurama kept his mother alive. He killed his mother and the world saw it. His sons were born and had energy, but his mother was not afraid of anything.
Ayodhya Kand.356: Unsuitable proper thoughts but which are stable. They dwell in the Lord who is ever blissful.
Ayodhya Kand.357: The patient king Bichan carried the burden of people, removed their sorrow. The king of Surapur was delighted. You say, O virtuous and excellent, there is no fault in virtue. All who are learned in the Vedas agree. He who gives receives the nectar. The king removes the noose, I say the deer finds benefit in respect. Hearing the sweet words of Rama, Baiden, no scholar says inappropriate words. All great ladies like Kausalya make the people happy. You, O Lord, are supreme, I know all this is good. Give me the king Rama, I will serve with affection.
Ayodhya Kand.358: Should the guest arrive while the minister is present, speak with emphasis. When Raghupati comes, do it at the right moment.
Ayodhya Kand.359: Kausalya with patience spoke. A son was born to the worthy couple. She respected this as beneficial. She understood the delay as the right time. Raghupati became the lord of men. You too are like this, dear, in worth. All the subjects, ministers, and relatives. You are the son for all to rely on. Writing the method, Bama endured the difficult times. With patience, Mother went ahead. Bowing to the guru, she followed. Protecting the subjects, she alleviated their pain. The guru rejoiced with the minister, hearing Bhartaris beneficial words. Mother spoke gently, with affection, simplicity, and pure essence.
Ayodhya Kand.360: Hearing the mother's words, full of pure, simple emotion, they became very distressed. Tears flowed from their lotus-like eyes, watering the new sprouts of separation in their hearts. Seeing that state, at that time, everyone forgot their bodily consciousness. Tulsidas praises everyone's respectful service and natural affection.
Ayodhya Kand.361: Hold India as a lotus, cherish her firmly and steadfastly. Save Bharam and give him the appropriate answer immediately.
Ayodhya Kand.362: I received this counsel from a good guru. The people and ministers are in agreement every morning. My mother placed me with the proper person. I wanted to wear the bracelet but did not. The guru, father, mother, and master speak for our benefit. Hearing this, my mind is pleased and I feel good. It is right to consider what is proper and improper. Following dharma, I carry the burden of sin on my head. You give me a simple teaching to follow. Whoever acts like me will be good. Even if I understand these, I cannot live in contentment. Now you listen to me without anger. I will recite and teach you. I will forgive the faults and praise the good.
Ayodhya Kand.363: O Surapura, you became so beautiful and charming that I fell in love with you. I know this is a great matter for you.
Ayodhya Kand.364: Hit has a siyahi sevaki. So hari leinhu mata kutilai I have seen a man in the fish. An upayon mor hit nahiṁ Seek understanding and write some advice. Read Lakhan Ram Siya Binus poetry. Excessive adornment is a heavy burden. Excessive longing is a distraction from Brahman. A body is a temporary enjoyment. Without devotion to Hari, chanting and yoga are in vain. Without a soul, a body is meaningless. Excessive attachment to all is a burden. I wish to be a king and have my desires fulfilled. Savor excessive affection deeply within.
Ayodhya Kand.365: Kaikeyi, of crooked mind, turned away from Ram, shameless. You desire happiness, out of delusion, the kingdom of a wretch like me.
Ayodhya Kand.366: I say, the snake heard all and remained silent. I wish there were a righteous man. But I give my kingdom whenever I wish. I go to the netherworld whenever I wish. I live wherever sin resides. Wherever I stick like a creeper to Rama. I call Rama in the forest and stay in Amarpura. I consider all efforts futile. I sit and listen to everything attentively. Without Raghuvir, I am nowhere. I live with my life in jest. Rama is pure, the subject of love, the essence of joy. The earth trembles with desire for enjoyment. How can I express the hardness of the heart? Where the plot unfolds, wherever it expands.
Ayodhya Kand.367: Caran then says the work is very difficult but not for me. Kulis bones are tendons and steel bars very hard.
Ayodhya Kand.368: Kaikeyi, whose body is filled with evil intentions. May my life be taken before I am so unfortunate. If separation from the beloved is dear to life. I will see and hear much more now. Lakshman, Ram, and Sita were sent to the forest. They were sent for the benefit of the lord of Amaravati. She herself took widowhood and infamy. She gave sorrow and suffering to the people. She gave me happiness, good fame, and a good kingdom. Kaikeyi did all this. What good is there for me in this? You say, "Give a commentary on that." Born from Kaikeyi's womb in this world. It is not inappropriate for me to say this. My words are all made by fate. Why do you make the people five?
Ayodhya Kand.369: The disease of the planet again talks only that again hits behind. That disease strikes again and again, saying what treatment is there.
Ayodhya Kand.370: Whatever is worthy of hearing in the world about Kaikeyi. May the four-faced Brahma give that to me. Ram, the son of Dasaratha, is my younger brother. May fate give me great misfortune. You all say, "The commentary on the sandals." The king's command is good for everyone. How can I answer whom? Speak happily, as you wish. Leaving me with my evil mother. Who can say whose good it is? Who else in the animate and inanimate world. To whom Sita and Ram are not dear as life. Great loss for everyone is a great gain. My lowliness is not a fault, say. You are all bound by doubt, character, and love. Everything you say is appropriate.
Ayodhya Kand.371: Love is special when it is simple like Ramatu. I speak of sweet affection settling in me with humility.
Ayodhya Kand.372: Guru Vivekananda knows the world. Who equal the beauty of the whole universe. O Tilak, you are dressed in the best attire. None is so much against the other as you are. O Ram, leave this world of illusion. None can say I am not a devotee. I heard the sages words and accepted them with joy. In the end, I am there where water is. I am not afraid to say this world is deceitful. I do not think about the other world. One body has two doors. I am attached to Sita and Ram, causing sorrow. Life is a candle, Lakshman found a good match. None can say I am unworthy of Rams devotion. My life became part of Raghubir. I cannot say anything false, being unfortunate.
Ayodhya Kand.373: You speak of great humility, yet your head is not bowed. See how Raghunath attained the position without bowing down.
Ayodhya Kand.374: I have not thought of the next step. How can I understand without Raghubir?。 Fixed my gaze on one point, my mind is nowhere. I walk in the morning, Lord, I see you。。 Even if I am unworthy and a sinner。Fear is the reason for all my bonds。。 Yet I see refuge in your face. I beseech you to show special favor。。 I am simple and humble, yet not Ram。I am a child servant, yet a master。。 You consider me one of your five beloved peacocks。Come and give me your beautiful plumage。。 When I hear Binay, I understand. I come to Ramas capital again。。
Ayodhya Kand.375: Even though people are fickle, I am steadfast always and forever. I do not forsake you, O Raghubir.

Ayodhya Kand.452: The Gobasi male and female heard the divine message and engaged in devotion. Seeing the beauty and affection, all people became intoxicated and received the fruit.
Ayodhya Kand.453: Speak with a single mind. Ramu and Lakhanu are friends indeed. Bapas face turned red as he spoke. Seelus affection matched her graceful steps. Beṣu did not share his thoughts, nor did Sīy share her company. Ahead, the four moved with cunning. Not pleased, the mind was troubled. Friend, doubt arose, this was the confusion. Thus, in the heart, the third was believed. Speak, all is the same. Praise the words, worship the phrases. Speaking, Sapeṃ joined the conversation. Whatever form, Ram Rajs essence was broken. Much was praised, Seelus affection, beautiful and fair.
Ayodhya Kand.454: Wandering pilgrims, sweet fruit, father gives to son, thus Raju. Coming to mind Raghuvir, Bharat son of Raghu.
Ayodhya Kand.455: Faith fills the heart with devotion and good conduct. He speaks and listens to remove pain and pollution. Whoever speaks a little, O friend, may Ram be his companion and not alone. We all see the blessed ones. They are written as fortunate by the people. Hearing the virtues, the servant follows. Kaki the mother had no son. Some say the queen is not polluted. We are all the right side as per destiny. We are the poor, ignorant, and weak. We live in begging, nurturing, and supporting. Where is this sight of good results and merit. Without joy and eternal, we are like trees in a desert land.
Ayodhya Kand.456: While watching Bharat Darshu, the eyes open wide. It is as if Singhlabasini easily shows the way.
Ayodhya Kand.457: With his own virtues, Ram Gun Gatha. Hear and remember Raghunath while listening. Pilgrimage, sages, hermitages, divine abodes. Bow and immerse yourself in seeing them. In the heart, seek the heart of this one. Sweet like Padum, the affection of Ram. Meet Kirat Kol, become a servant. Sit like Bakhana, be sad like Bata. Bow and touch the feet wherever you see them. Sometimes become Lakhn, Ram in a playful mood. The Lord tells everything to everyone. Seeing this, the fruit of life is obtained. Whoever sees Kusal, Ram and Lakhn are the same. From this, everyone understands the beautiful story. Hearing Ram, become a listener to the story.
Ayodhya Kand.458: Stay seated until morning, remembering Sumri and Raghunath. Longing for Ram's vision fills the hearts of all.
Ayodhya Kand.459: Auspicious omens occurred for everyone. Joyful eyes and arms twitched. The society, along with Bharati, was enthusiastic. Ram will meet them, and the burning pain of sorrow will end. Everyone made wishes in their hearts. They were all intoxicated with love. Their limbs were weak, their feet stumbled on the path. They spoke in choked voices, overcome by love. At that time, Ram's friend showed them the naturally beautiful chief of mountains. Near it, on the bank of the river, where the two brothers resided together. Everyone bowed down, saying, 'Victory to Janaki's life, Ram!'
Ayodhya Kand.460: Bharat's love at that time, Sheshnag could not describe it. Just as the bliss of Brahman is inaccessible to poets, so it is to my impure knowledge.
Ayodhya Kand.461: All affection is weak, Raghubar is the center. Went two days, stayed three nights. Saw the ups and downs, passed the night. The government of Raghunath is pleasing. Night and day, remained content. Stayed awake, saw dreams. The society brought people together. Lord, the union, pain, the body. All the mind is dirty, sorrowful. Saw the mother, affectionate. Heard Sitas dream, filled with tears. Became thinking, thinking, released. Lakhns dream, this is not good. Hard, some tell the truth. Saying this, bathed with friends. Worshipped the ancient, praised the saint.
Ayodhya Kand.462: The sun, the gods, sages, and prisoners sat waiting to see the answer. The sky filled with dust, birds, and many animals, and at midday, the lord visited his hermitage. Tulsidas stood observing, wondering why he remained conscious and aware. He received all news and messages, and that became his opportunity.
Ayodhya Kand.463: Hearing the auspicious words, the mind was filled with joy, and the body thrilled. Tulasi's eyes, like autumn lotuses, filled with tears of love.
Ayodhya Kand.464: Again, Ram became thoughtful. "What is the reason for Bharat's arrival in the forest?" One person came and said again, "He has a small four-fold army with him." Hearing this, Ram became very worried. On one side, the father's word, on the other, the brother's hesitation. Understanding Bharat's nature in his mind, the Lord could not find a favorable position for his thoughts. Then he found a solution, knowing this: "Bharat is among the saints and wise." Lakshman saw the Lord's heart was troubled. He spoke words of policy appropriate for the time. "Without asking, what can I say, Lord? It is not the time for a servant's impudence. You are the omniscient, the crown jewel of masters. Your own."
Ayodhya Kand.465: Friendship with a gentle heart, simplicity, virtue, and affection are treasures. You appear as love to all, knowing you is like knowing yourself.
Ayodhya Kand.466: Fiery living beings rule the realm. Foolish delusion only befalls the people. True conduct holds the wise and knowledgeable. Understanding the Lords place, love encompasses all the world. Today, I have attained the feet of Rama. I shall go and extinguish the wicked. The opportune moment for evil is a trap. Knowing Rama, I remain alone. I adorn my mind with sacred mantras. Come, let me be the unblemished king. Countless forms of deceit are devised. Come, let the group uproot the two brothers. If one is born, let it not be deceit. Sometimes one rides the chariot, sometimes the elephant. I give my dear friend what he should receive. The world honors the kings position.
Ayodhya Kand.467: The moon went to the Guru's wife, Nahusha ascended to the Brahmin's palanquin. Turning away from the world and Vedas, the wicked became like Vena.
Ayodhya Kand.468: Sahasbahu, Suranath, Trisanku. Which king has not been defiled by the intoxication of power? Bharat has done this appropriate deed. No one will keep the enemy, debt, or stain. Why is Bharat not good? Ram, knowing him helpless, feared him. Today, especially, they will face him. Seeing Ram's angry face in battle. Saying this much, he forgot the essence of policy. The tree of battle's passion blossomed with the excuse of thrill. Bowing at the Lord's feet, he kept his head on the ground. He spoke with natural strength and truth. 'Lord, do not consider my words inappropriate. Bharat has not given us little treatment. How long can we suppress our minds? Lord, with you, the bow is in our hands.'
Ayodhya Kand.469: The tribe of women, Raghuvelas Janamrutha, followers of Rama, know this world. Strike with the palm, raise the head, strike the head of the lowly, consider it equal.
Ayodhya Kand.470: Rise and cry out for the queens help. My mind is awake with the valor of the hero. Binding the hair, cutting the beard, dressing in armor, and preparing the hands. Today, as a servant of Ram, I will take. Teach the art of war, I will impart. Seeing Ram, the fruit of disrespect was obtained. Sleeping in war, the two brothers were awakened. Come and become a good member of the society. Manifest today, I will reveal the hidden. Like the deer king, emerging and capturing the deer. Thus, with the army, he is included. Sankaru falls, he is struck in the field. Helping, the tangle of confusion comes. Then I will strike and defeat Ram in duels.
Ayodhya Kand.471: Very eager Makha Lakhnu went following the path heard. Full of fear, he desired to be the lord of all people.
Ayodhya Kand.472: Fear shakes the sky, words tremble in the air. Lakhna, the mighty, marvels at the vast. Your father, Pratap, is. Who can describe him, who can see him clearly? Some actions are fitting, some are not. Understand and praise well whoever you can. Haste brings regret, even Bed and Buddha cannot help. Hearing the sound, Lakhna trembled, Ram Siya honored him with respect. Your advice, father, is good. All are hard, royal madness brothers. Those who are just kings are they. There is no assembly of the righteous where they are. Listen, Lakhna, you are well, the best of the best. I have heard the world, the universe, but not your like.
Ayodhya Kand.473: Do you not have faith in the words of the Lord? Indeed, some have perished without Bhakti (devotion) like the chaff in a storm.
Ayodhya Kand.474: Let darkness swallow the young sun. Let the sky merge with the clouds. Let Agastya drown in a cow's hoof-print water. Let the earth abandon its natural patience. Let a mosquito blow away Mount Meru. But let not Bharat be intoxicated by royal power, O brother. Lakshman, I swear by you and by father, there is no pure brother like Bharat. Virtues are like milk, and faults are like water, O father. The creator mixed them to create the world. Bharat, like a swan in the pond of the solar dynasty, was born and separated the good from the bad. He took the milk (virtues) and left the water (faults). He illuminated his fame in the world. Saying Bharat is like a swan.
Ayodhya Kand.475: Hearing Raghuvir's words, Bharat became bewildered. Ram praised everything and blessed the Lord as a favor.
Ayodhya Kand.476: O Lord, without Thee, the world is empty. All religions bear and support Thee. The poet sings the glory of Kula Agam. Without Thee, none can know Raghunath. Listening to the divine words of Lakhan Ram Sita, one feels immense joy; it is not to be described. Here, all are supported together. Bathing in the Mandakini and Punyabhumi. Placing the river nearby, all people meet their mothers and gurus for appointments. Joining Sita and Raghuram, even the small brothers go. Understanding this, mothers get worried. Thinking and planning, countless thoughts arise in the mind. Listening to Lakhan and Sita, I feel my name is Ram. Rising, I live forever, wherever Sita and Raghuram are.
Ayodhya Kand.477: Mother thinks whatever her child does is right. Understanding her childs way, she sees no flaw.
Ayodhya Kand.478: Flee from the polluted mind, know the servant as the Lord. O birds, seek shelter in Ram, the Lord is the master and friend to all. The world is full of singers, some are skilled, some are novices. With such a mind, it wanders, with love it sings everything. Turning the mind towards the mother, it becomes a devoted heart. Moving with devotion, it gains strength, patience, and courage. When one understands Raghunath as excellent, the path becomes clear. Bharata, the son of Dasaratha, was such an opportunity. Like the flow of water, like the flow of the river Ali, so is the life of Bharata. Seeing Bharata, I thought of love, the Nishad time has passed.
Ayodhya Kand.479: He is attracted to the auspicious qualities, hearing and praising them as a outcaste. Thinking and becoming happy, again he becomes sorrowful.
Ayodhya Kand.480: The servant lives, known by all for truth. Go near the Ashram, Niranjan. Bharat sees the society as a sal forest. The people are delighted, as if they have found a good ruler. The people are distressed, suffering from fear and disease. The three types of suffering afflict the household. The king is happy in his own country. Bharat's condition is similar to that. Ram's residence has become Bharat's wealth. The people are happy, as if they have found a good king. The minister is detachment, the king is wisdom. The forest is a beautiful and sacred land. The soldiers are Yama and Niyama, the capital is the sal tree. Peace, good sense, and purity are the beautiful queen. The king is complete in all his limbs. His heart is eager, devoted to Ram's feet.
Ayodhya Kand.481: King Viveka won with the army of King Moha. He distributed happiness and wealth in his undisputed kingdom.
Ayodhya Kand.482: In this vast region, many sages reside. It is as if there are many cities, towns, and villages. There are numerous diverse birds and deer. The assembly of creatures cannot be described. Birds hunt and tigers roar. Buffaloes and bulls graze together. Forgetting their enmity, they move together. Here and there, it is as if the four divisions of the army are present. Waterfalls cascade, and intoxicated elephants trumpet. It is as if various kinds of drums are playing. Chakors, cuckoos, parrots, and nightingales sing. Beautiful swans sing with joyful hearts. Bees hum and peacocks dance. It is as if there is good governance and auspiciousness all around. Creepers, trees, and grasses are all fruitful and flowering. All are equal.
Ayodhya Kand.483: Bharat saw the beauty of Ram's forest dwelling, and his heart was filled with immense love. Just as ascetics are pleased and refreshed upon receiving the fruit of their penance.
Ayodhya Kand.484: Then Kevat climbed the high hills and said, Bhartu lifted his arms. I saw the dense forest, filled with jambu, rasala, and tamala trees. On the tree branches, in the middle, I saw the beautiful leaves. The beautiful leaves captivated my mind. The deep green leaves and the red fruits. The evergreen shade, a blissful place at all times. I saw the twilight and sunrise, mixed in colors. One tree near the stream, Gosains shadow. Under Raghuvirs canopy, where it casts its shadow. Tulsi trees, in various forms, pleasing to see. Sometimes Siya, sometimes Lakhman, came here. The tree shadows, bedika made. Siya, her own water, lotus pleasing.
Ayodhya Kand.485: Seated there, Munigana along with Niti recited the story of Sita, Ramu Sujan. Hearing the narrative of the past and the new.
Ayodhya Kand.486: Brother on hearing the news, Bihari looked surprised. Bhargava filled with emotion, Bilochan came quickly. Bowing, the two brothers walked. Saying, Sardar Prem teased. Seeing Ramas feet, Paras smiled. Holding Rajs head, Hyan made his eyes moist. Meeting Raghubir was a great joy. Watching Bharat go, Prems heart was filled with an excessive love. Brothers affection, Bibas forgot. Saying, Sur showered auspicious flowers. Seeing the saintly, devoted, Anurag felt natural affection. Bharat was not a mere mortal, Raghubir was both constant and changeable.
Ayodhya Kand.487: Love is the Mandara mountain, separation is the ocean. Bharat churned it, and for the welfare of gods and saints, the ocean of compassion, Raghubir, appeared.
Ayodhya Kand.488: Brother and charming companion together. Lakhewal without Lakhna dense did not become. Bharat appears, Lord in the holy hermitage. All auspicious, sumptuous dwelling delights. Service removes the claim of suffering. Janu, the yogi, attained supreme bliss. I see Bharat, Lakhna, Lord ahead. I ask, tell me, my beloved. The muni shaved his beard, tied his cloth. How can I do, my simple hands. Yogis and sages, society together. With a wife, King Raghus royal family. Body, dark, complex, the munis form. Janu, the muni, took pleasure in the yogis form. The muni, with a snake, turned the bow. His smile, like a flower, saw the laughter.
Ayodhya Kand.489: Let the beautiful sage reside in the shade of Raghuchandra. The body of the assembly of wise people is sustained by devotion to Sachchidananda.
Ayodhya Kand.490: Anuj is a friend, a companion of the mind. Forgotten are joy, sorrow, happiness, and pain. Look, Lord, look, Guru Gosai. From the ground to the sky, a mere speck. Living, knowing, Lakhna recognizes. Bowing in service, knowing life and death. Friend, affection, this ones way. Master, service, this ones strength. Meeting is not possible, nor becoming a burden. Lakhnas mind, a fleeting thought. Staying, preserving service, a heavy burden. Climbing, reaching, cutting, playing. Saying, loving, not in the heart. Bowing in service to Raghunatha. Rising, Ram, hearing the call. Saying, whispering, silent, sharp arrow.
Ayodhya Kand.491: I raised Barbas from his bed as a favor. I forgot the whole morning, seeing the meeting of Bharat and Ram.
Ayodhya Kand.492: Meeting and love how to describe with praise. Poetic skill and art in the hearts speech. True love and fulfillment for both brothers. Mind and wisdom forgotten in self-realization. Say true love openly and clearly shown. Sometimes shadow follows the wise mind. Poetic meaning in the end is a hint. Rhythm and movement in the dance of life. Unconditional love fills the Raghubirs heart. Where the heart does not go, the mind seeks Hari. I call myself foolish in any way. Like a bulls hide, the skin is tough. Meeting and sight fill the Raghubirs heart. Radiant beauty in the assembly, shaking and trembling. Teach the Suraguru, awaken the root. Rain of pleasure, joyous sound.
Ayodhya Kand.493: I can smell the Ripusudani herb on Ram's body. Bharat, with great fear, prostrated before Lakshman.
Ayodhya Kand.494: When Lakhna Lalki came, he was a small brother. Beyond Nishad, he was brought up. When Punhi Mungani came, we were like brothers. Such a joy in such a meeting. With great affection, Bharat embraced Dharma. With his head, he touched the feet of Sita. Again and again, he stood up in reverence. He sat down, his hands like lotus petals. Sita, the beloved of Rama, gave her heart and soul. Her love was not shallow. All the ways, Sita wrote with joy. She spent her life without hesitation. Sometimes he said something, sometimes he remained silent. His heart filled with love, he touched his own soul. With patience, he waited for the right moment. Without hesitation, he offered his life in devotion.
Ayodhya Kand.495: Nath was with Muninath, his maternal uncle, all the people. The sevaks, senap, and sachiv all came in the afternoon twilight.
Ayodhya Kand.496: Hearing the conch from the guru, the warriors grew fierce. Keeping enemies close, they kept peace nearby. All went with Rama, the black one. Steadfast in duty, the merciful one. Seeing the guru, the son felt affection. Bowing in reverence, they touched the feet of the Lord. The sage took hold of his heart. Meeting his beloved, the two brothers embraced. The beloved pulsed, the name was said. These distances were bridged in reverence. Rama the friend met the sage. Janu won the sages affection. Raghupati, with devotion, became the root of happiness. The heavens welcomed the melody of the gods. None is lower in this equality. None is greater among the sages in the world.
Ayodhya Kand.497: Whoever writes and recites more will be blessed and praised. So let it be known through the spread of Sitapatis hymn.
Ayodhya Kand.498: Rats people know Ram Subu. Karunakar Sujan Bhagwana. Whoever was eager to stay alive. He kept that alive in every way. Sanoj met everyone in a moment. Such great distance caused great pain. This is a great matter, Ram doesnt know. Like a thousand events, one desire. Meeting with Kevatihu, with love. Everyone praised the pure person. I saw Ram, a sad lady. She was like a snow-covered hill. First, Ram met Cakkei. Simple, good, faith, mind met. Waking up, Keinbhodhu, great joy. White, black, good deeds, head held high.
Ayodhya Kand.499: Raghubar mata taught all at the assembly, enlightening Paritosh. Amba was always blameless, under her supervision.
Ayodhya Kand.500: The brave hero, brother Duhu, with Bhipati who joined him. Gangoari is equal to all noble ones. Dehini Asis spoke gentle words. Gahis feet were marked by Sumitra. Janu met with wealth beyond measure. Again, Janani and Charanani, the two brothers, were agitated. Intense affection was brought to his heart. Tears of affection flowed from his eyes. Thus, he was happy and sad at the same time. Like a mute poet, he expressed joy and sorrow. Meeting Janani and Saniu, Ragurao, Gur said, they are the bearers of the order. People flowed from everywhere like water from the earth to the sky.
Ayodhya Kand.501: The minister of Mahisur joined the people who went to listen to the guru. Pawan Ashram was visited by Bhargava Lakhn and Raghunath.
Ayodhya Kand.502: The lady of beauty touched my heart. Truly worthy, she won my affection. With the Gurus grace and the Saints company. Meeting her, I found what I could not find. Bonded bond, the lady is with every step. Cherishing her, I long for my beloved. When all ladies saw the beauty. Their eyes filled with admiration, young and old. The fair one sat in my heart, dying within. Why should I grieve, when she is here? Seeing her, I found relief from pain. Truly, she is the help I sought. Janakas son, with calmness, held her.
